quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Section 21 meets our preferred position. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of 12 months' Fees "paid or payable" and USD 1,000,000; "Fees" (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the base is not illusory. Section 21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (and helpfully confirms restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages, which favours us). Section 21.3 carves out, uncapped, breach of confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages". Section 18.2 further confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liability. No one-sided or sub-6-month cap and no indemnity inside the cap, so no redline is warranted.

ops.text:
20. INDEMNIFICATION
20.1 Vendor shall defend and indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
20.2 Customer's indemnity obligations under this Agreement are limited to third-party claims arising out of (a) content or materials provided by Customer to Vendor; or (b) Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
20.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim; the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defence of the claim; and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation.

proposal.summary: Insert a concise new Section 20 (Indemnification) at the preferred position: Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for IP, breach-of-law, data-breach and misconduct claims, with notice/control/cooperation procedure and a narrow Customer indemnity.

quote: “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property.
rationale: The Agreement contains no indemnification clause at all. Section 20 is absent from the document: searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "defend" return only incidental references that presuppose an indemnity that was never drafted — Section 9.3 cross-references remedies "required by Section 20.5", Section 19.4 carves out "indemnified claims", Section 21.3 makes "indemnification obligations" an Excluded Claim, and Section 30.5 preserves "vested indemnity rights". With no Vendor IP indemnity anywhere, this is walk-away territory under the rule and fails both the preferred and fallback positions. We inserted a new Section 20 at the preferred position: Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard notice/control/cooperation procedure; customary exclusions and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies at 20.5 (which also cures the dangling cross-reference in 9.3); and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. No super-cap is needed since Section 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims.

proposal.summary: Negate the Customer-side disclose-and-match MFN obligation in Section 7.2 so no MFN duty binds Customer.

quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
rationale:
Section 7.2 (first instance) imposes an MFN-style obligation on Customer, not Vendor: before engaging any other provider we must disclose any more favourable commercial offer we receive and match it for Vendor. This is unlimited as to product, duration, and comparability, with no reasonable-comparison carve-outs, so it fails the fallback (defined product, 12 months, carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory as an open-ended duty to extend Vendor better third-party terms. It also conflicts with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. The minimal fix is deletion of the Customer-side obligation; any Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would be retained.</parationale>

quote: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
rationale: Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) addresses only access cut-off after "any agreed transition period", Deliverable delivery and Fee refunds. There is no obligation on Vendor to provide transition/migration assistance, to return or export Customer Data in a usable format, or to delete and certify deletion. Section 16.5 expressly carves Customer Data out of the confidentiality return/destroy mechanic and defers it to "Sections 11 and 15" — but no Section 11 exists in the document and Section 15 covers processing limits and privacy only, not exit. Searches for data return/export/deletion language return nothing. This is a hosted-services agreement, so the absence fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus 30-day export). Proposed insertion of a new Section 10.3 matching the preferred position (up to 6 months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion, with a routine-backup/legal-retention carve-out consistent with Section 16.5).
